messages:
Maria: Heads-up — we need to finalize the error taxonomy + dashboard matrix for the new rollout. Focus: timeouts, 5xx, OOMs, degraded-mode/fallback counts, and routing-induced errors. Who's around for a quick sync?

Raj: I'm in. can share runtime-level counters we already emit. quick ask: do we want rate (per-sec) or ratio (%) vs requests?

Lina: ratio is more actionable for ML teams — we care about degraded-mode percentage per model and per route. absolute counts still useful for SRE.

Tom: Agree — SRE wants both. counts for alerting (>= threshold) and ratios for dashboards/SLOs. Also need clear labels: model, route, pool, region, rollout_tag.

Maria: Proposed minimal metric set (names tentative):
```
redwood_requests_total{route,model,pool,region}
redwood_latency_p95_ms{route,model,pool}
redwood_errors_5xx_total{route,model,pool,region,rollout}
redwood_errors_timeout_total{route,model,pool,region,rollout}
redwood_errors_oom_total{route,model,pool,region}
redwood_fallbacks_degraded_total{route,model,pool,reason,rollout}
redwood_routing_to_fallbacks_total{route,from_pool,to_pool,reason}
```

Raj: Those look good. A couple notes from runtime: we can emit oom & timeout at the worker level and aggregate at the router; but routing->fallbacks is only known at the gateway when it decides to re-route. We should add a unique request_id label to correlate when debugging.

Sam: For Console UX, we want prebuilt panels: 1) global error heatmap, 2) per-route SLO burn rate, 3) rollout comparison (new vs canary). We also want drill-down links that open the request traces.

Zoe: Product: can we show fallback reason breakdown in the route overview? customers care why model was downgraded (quota, oom, timeout, cold-start).

Lina: Add reason label values: oom, timeout, high_queue, capacity_quota, model_mismatch, runtime_error. Keep the label set bounded.

Tom: Alerting rules proposal:
- P1: sustained redwood_errors_oom_total increase > 0 for 5m on any pool -> pager
- P1: redwood_errors_5xx_total / redwood_requests_total > 3% for 10m for a key route -> pager
- P2: degraded_mode_rate (fallbacks / requests) > 1% for 15m for enterprise routes -> slack alert

Maria: Can we standardize metric suffixes: _total for counters, _gauge for instantaneous values, and histograms for latency?

Raj: yes. runtime already uses _total for counters. we'll expand labels to include rollout (vX) and customer_tier. Need to watch cardinality for model label (we have hundreds) — propose model_id truncated to first 8 chars.

Lina: Truncation is fine but make sure Console joins to downstream metadata table for full model name.

Sam: For dashboards we need pre-aggregated rollup metrics to avoid heavy queries: e.g., redwood_errors_5xx_by_route_5m which is a recording rule for increase(redwood_errors_5xx_total[5m]). Will that work?

Raj: Absolutely — we'll add recording rules at the infra prometheus layer. Also add recording for fallback_ratio_5m = increase(redwood_fallbacks_degraded_total[5m]) / increase(redwood_requests_total[5m]).

Tom: Debates: where to count timeouts? router vs worker. If worker times out after work started, it should increment worker.timeout. But gateway-level truncated requests (client disconnects) are different — need distinct labels: origin:worker|gateway.

Maria: Good call. add origin label.

Zoe: Rollouts UX question: can we surface a side-by-side for canary vs baseline showing p95 latency, 5xx rate, fallback rate? Also a small sparkline for the last 1h.

Sam: We'll add a 'rollout compare' widget with configurable windows (5m/1h/24h). It will pull recording rules per rollout tag.

Lina: Implementation note: ML runtime can emit a lightweight event for degraded inference that contains model_version + fallback_reason and we can route into event pipeline (kafka) for richer analysis (percentiles by input size etc). This avoids high cardinality in metrics.

Raj: good plan — metrics for SLOs, events for deep dive.

Tom: Can we agree on metric naming conventions and labels in a short doc PR? I'd like a single source of truth before we wire dashboards.

Maria: I'll open a docs PR with the proposed names, labels, and alert thresholds. Assigning tasks: Raj -> expose recording rules + origin label by EOD Tue. Lina -> emit degraded events to kafka prototype by Wed. Sam -> mock Console panels and rollout compare by Thu. Tom -> draft alerting rules and runbook by Thu. Zoe -> mapping of customer routes that need enterprise thresholds by Fri.

Raj: noted. I'll also add example PromQL for the panels: 
```
# 5xx rate 5m
increase(redwood_errors_5xx_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m]) / increase(redwood_requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m]) * 100

# fallback ratio 5m
increase(redwood_fallbacks_degraded_total[5m]) / increase(redwood_requests_total[5m]) * 100
```

Sam: pinging @DeployBot to create a dashboard ticket with the new recording rules so infra can pick it up.

DeployBot: Dashboard ticket created: DB-4821 — includes recording rule names and panel templates. :white_check_mark:

Maria: Thanks everyone. If there are no objections I'll merge the doc PR after comments are in. Please add any edge cases here (cold starts, prewarm failures, quota-denied)

Lina: Edge case: model fallback due to quantization mismatch vs model architecture mismatch — label as model_mismatch.

Tom: Edge case: OOM while serving long-context requests -> tag with seq_len_bucket label. Keep buckets coarse (<=512, 513-2048, >2048).

Raj: Also surface routing policy tag: route_policy=latency|cost|tier so we can correlate degradations when cost-based routing kicks in.

Maria: Great. I'll include these in the PR. thanks :tada:

Zoe: :thumbsup:
